column1: # STEPS.tsv -- THE DESIGN-PLAN run-switches STEP TABLE: THE SCRIP SIDE OF THE CLEAN-UP OF THE SIX MASTERS AND OF corpus/packages (the cto, CTO-575, 2026-11-10, TRIO, the design-only phase; Lon in the cio's window 11:1x CST, verbatim: "We also need major clean up in the $/corpus/packages language folders just like the tests folder but they will not have ONE LINERS and MULTI LINERS. Instead the programs will have the same layout as in the distribution from which it came, and side-by-side files with NAME.in, NAME.out, and NAME.err files. And slightly varying ALL files."; the package index, NAME.in beside a program and ALL.args at the package root as the cio rules them in CIO-59 and CIO-60). The design text is skill suites-and-grading reference section 8.

# harness/scripts/test_design_run_switches_steps.sh reads it: --list prints it; --step N runs the step's PROBE, bash harness/scripts/s4e_probe_run_switches.sh N, from S4E_HOME. A probe builds its own containers and packages in scratch, cuts every expected text from the language's oracle (fpc live in step 3; the batch-grader Prolog witnesses' swipl answers in step 8; the two rs11 witnesses beside this table, cut twice from swipl -q -t halt and from XSB 5.0.0 on 2026-11-10) and reads RED, never REFUSED, while SCRIP lacks the switch or the column it asks for.

# probe tokens: none; each probe is the whole measurement (rc 0 GREEN, 1 RED, 2 could not measure). MEASURED RED on 2026-11-10 at SCRIP 08c716738, corpus 2d085b730, harness 21201d36: every step 1 to 12; steps 13 and 14 (CTO-583: the package switch reads ALL.source and ALL.launch, the cio's CIO-83, CIO-92, CIO-93, CIO-96) MEASURED RED at harness 29b5bedd.

# THE NAMES A STEP MAY NOT CHANGE, because a probe reads them: the index columns dialect, stage_name, path (named file until CIO-113 (3a), 2026-11-10: the Pascal indexes already carry a feature column named file, so the package index's column is path, directly after entry; the cto's step 9 landing renamed it in the probes), grader; the accessor oracle_cmd_for LANG DIALECT in lib_oracle_flags.sh and its table harness/scripts/oracle_dialects.tsv; the driver function scrip_warm_prolog; the warm line on standard error, scrip: --run-multi-liners warm lang=prolog procs=N (--run-one-liners and --harness say their own switch name); the switch --run-files DIR --out OUT [--only FILE] [--work DIR]; the Prolog dialect name swi.

# NO ROW IS SERVED until Lon lifts the idle of 2026-11-10 (CIO-58): every row is minted FREE, owned by the cto, in no tube. Step 6 is the first SCRIP step the cto asks Lon to lift: the prelude's planning and emission is nine tenths of a Prolog test's processor time (hello.pl 0.79 s user against 0.005 s for the other languages).
